prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "dalleserver", with the standing line "A small web server that turns an Ethereum address and a chosen series into a consistently generated, annotated image, reporting progress as it works." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows An address enters at upper left as a written string beside a series name. It passes a validation gate, then a cache check. At the cache check, a short branch leads straight to the finished image. The main path passes through a padlocked generation lock and then down eight connected stations in order: setup, base prompts, enhance prompt, image prep, image wait, image download, annotate, completed. Arrows run only forward, and the path ends at the annotated PNG in .

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows the circuit breaker as a switch with three positions, where the open position routes enhancement back to the original prompt. The second circle shows several requests arriving at one padlock, with only one run passing through. The third circle shows a file written to a temporary name and then renamed. holds three studies: a progress snapshot card with a filling bar, a 42-character address being checked, and a series acting as a filter over prompt attributes.

Colour is used so that Warm ochre marks the main generation path. Green marks the cache-hit shortcut. Muted red marks failure and fallback routes.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: The pipeline has eight phases from setup to completed. The address is 42 characters, beginning 0x. Five consecutive failures open the circuit breaker, and two successes close it again. Five prompt texts are saved beside each image.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: series goes on the filter set. The annotated PNG is the final watermarked image. enhanced is the prompt text rewritten by the LLM. data, title, and terse are the prompt folders. ?generate=1 starts or forces a run. ?remove=1 deletes the annotated PNG. /preview is the gallery. progress snapshot is the JSON returned while a run is working. done marks completion. cacheHit marks the shortcut path. circuit breaker protects enhancement. generation lock is keyed by series and address.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: Ethereum address, series, validate, cache check, generation lock, setup, base prompts, enhance prompt, image prep, image wait, image download, annotate. circuit breaker, closed, half-open, open, original prompt. progress snapshot, percent, ETA, done. annotated PNG, data, title, terse, enhanced, /preview. ?generate=1, ?remove=1.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: An existing image is served at once; duplicate requests share one locked run. Five failures open the breaker; enhancement failure falls back to original prompt. Poll the same address until done; percent and ETA learn from past runs. Prompts stay when the image is removed. Without a key, image generation is skipped.
